newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Waigel says no new spending in EU jobs resolution.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says no new spending in EU jobs resolution.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that the employment resolution agreed earlier by EU finance ministers involved no additional spending.
Reporting to journalists after the ministers' meeting, he said: "The employment resolution is so arranged that no additional financial resources are involved."
Supporting the case for a special employment summit to look into what the European Union can do to cut its jobless queues, he said, "Nobody can have anything against a jobs summit".
On the jobs and growth resolution, he said, "We can live happily with that, including the resolution on growth and jobs, because it involves no extra resources."
There would be no additional volume in European Investment Bank credits and EIB profits would flow into the bank's equity, he said.
In the context of the jobs resolution and the stability pact there had also been no question of exchange-rate oriented measures to limit employment, he said.

Waigel told reporters that the stability pact aimed at ensuring financial discipline within monetary union would be adopted unchanged from its original form by the Amsterdam summit, despite French protests in advance of the meeting that they may need more time to consider the pact before agreeing it.
"The stability pact can be adopted unchanged as can the ERM2 and the legal status of the euro," he said.
